stem: Kavya says, 'Asha is the wife of my brother Ravi. Ravi's father Mohan is my father. Ravi and I have no other siblings.' How is Kavya related to Asha?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Asha is the wife of Kavya's brother Ravi. The wife of one's sibling is one's sister-in-law. So Kavya is Asha's sister-in-law (from Asha's perspective, Kavya is the sister of her husband Ravi).
Sister would mean Asha and Kavya share parents. Asha married into the family; she is not a blood sister of Kavya.
Daughter-in-law is the wife of one's son. Kavya is Ravi's sister, not Ravi's mother, so Asha cannot be Kavya's daughter-in-law.
Cousin requires the parents to be siblings of each other. Asha is Ravi's wife, not a blood relative, so there is no cousin relationship between Kavya and Asha.

explanation: Kavya and Ravi are siblings (same father Mohan, no other siblings). Asha is Ravi's wife. The wife of Kavya's brother is Kavya's sister-in-law.

explanation_sections.punchline: Wife of a sibling = sister-in-law; the direction from Kavya to Asha is straightforward once the sibling link is established.
explanation_sections.approach: Apply clues most-certain-first: Ravi is Kavya's brother (same father, no other siblings confirmed). Asha is Ravi's wife => Asha is Kavya's sister-in-law (Kavya is Asha's sister-in-law from Asha's viewpoint too).
explanation_sections.lesson: The wife of your brother is your sister-in-law; your relation to her mirrors her relation to you.
explanation_sections.timing: About 45 seconds. This is straightforward once the sibling link is noted. The trap is option 2 (sister), treating a married-in member as a blood sibling.
